chunks: And from him, from Al-Husayn, from An-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Madaini, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "When you fast, let your hearing and your sight fast from the forbidden and the ugly; avoid quarreling and the annoyance of the servant, and let the dignity of fasting be upon you, and do not make your day of fasting like your day of breaking the fast."
ai.seo_question: What are the ethical and sensory requirements of fasting according to Imam Al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates fasting from mere physical abstinence to a holistic discipline of the senses, warning that hearing and sight must also fast from prohibited matters. He specifically highlights social ethics by commanding the avoidance of quarreling and mistreating servants, ensuring the spiritual dignity (*waqar*) of the fast permeates daily interactions. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on *sawm al-jarih* (fasting of the limbs) as essential for the acceptance of the ritual.
